requirement: Collect NFL betting lines (point spread, moneyline, total) for every scheduled game each week.
rationale: Line generation depends on a complete, current slate of market prices to compare against generated signals.

requirement: Collect opening and closing line values for every bet to compute Closing Line Value (CLV).
rationale: CLV measures whether the price taken beat the price at kickoff — the core skill signal that removes luck.

requirement: Pull official team standings (W/L/T, points for/against) as a baseline performance input.
rationale: Standings anchor strength-of-team baselines used by every signal.

requirement: Pull official team offensive and defensive team stats (passing/rushing/scoring).
rationale: Offensive and defensive efficiency stats are the raw inputs for line projection models.

requirement: Pull official NFL injury reports per team per week (questionable/doubtful/out).
rationale: Injury status directly shifts projected performance and is required by the injury-tracking requirement.

requirement: Pull official transactions and reserve-list moves (IR, reserve/injured, designations).
rationale: Reserve-list moves confirm which starters are unavailable and force backups into starting roles.

requirement: Pull team depth charts to know starter and 2nd/3rd/4th-string ordering at every position.
rationale: Depth charts let the system identify which backup is replacing an injured starter and quantify the deficiency.

requirement: Generate original NFL line projections (projected spread, total, and win probability) rather than copying market lines.
rationale: The goal is to originate own lines and find value against the market, not to echo the books.

requirement: Develop signal-generation strategies for single bets (side, total, moneyline).
rationale: Single-bet strategies are the baseline building block and the cleanest place to measure skill.

requirement: Develop signal-generation strategies for parlays (multi-leg combinations).
rationale: Parlays combine multiple signals; they require correlation handling to avoid false edge from correlated legs.

requirement: Develop signal-generation strategies for player proposition (prop) bets and prop combos.
rationale: Player props are a distinct market the user explicitly requested; they need dedicated signals.

requirement: Require every strategy to pass a set of validation gates before it is accepted or ranked.
rationale: Validation gates prevent lucky, overfit, or data-leakage strategies from entering the leaderboard.

requirement: Compute correlation values between markets/legs before building parlay and prop combos.
rationale: Correlation determines whether combined legs are genuinely diversifying or double-counting the same risk.

requirement: Remove luck by ranking strategies on CLV and out-of-sample edge, not short-term win rate.
rationale: Win rate is dominated by variance; CLV isolates the skill of price-finding.

requirement: Build strategies that are selectively skill-based — taking fewer, higher-conviction bets rather than betting every game.
rationale: Selectivity reduces variance and focuses edge on the highest-conviction signals.

requirement: Track injuries and translate them into projected lineup impact per team per week.
rationale: Injuries are the primary driver of line movement and must be tracked systematically, not manually.

requirement: Detect defensive deficiencies where 2nd, 3rd, or 4th-string backups must replace starters.
rationale: Backup defenders replacing starters degrade defensive performance and move lines; this must be quantified.

requirement: Detect offensive deficiencies where starters are replaced by backups at skill and line positions.
rationale: Backup offensive starters (QB/RB/WR/OL) change offensive output and must be tracked the same way as defense.

requirement: Cross-reference injury status with depth charts to name the specific backup elevating to starter.
rationale: Naming the elevating backup is what turns a status into an actionable, verifiable signal.

requirement: Publish a clean, simple, dashboard-style GitHub Pages site with a landing page and category subpages.
rationale: The user requested a clean, user-friendly dashboard with all entries and findings in readable tables.

requirement: Present all entries, findings, and analysis in simple, easy-to-read table format.
rationale: Tables make the data scannable and let every row carry its source link.

requirement: Include a dedicated Suggestions section where proposed improvements can be reviewed before implementation.
rationale: The user wants a review gate so the best path is chosen before any change is made.

requirement: Include an executive summary outlining the important details of the project.
rationale: The user explicitly requested an executive summary of key details.

requirement: Provide a clear list of questions, required information, and answers to address before decisions are made.
rationale: Decisions must be based on what is known and what is missing; the gap list drives discovery.

requirement: Make suggestions to discover missing information needed for decisions.
rationale: The user wants suggestions targeted at filling information gaps, not just feature ideas.

requirement: Verify every table row against an official source; leave unconfirmed values blank and flag them.
rationale: No hallucinations — unverified values must never be inferred or filled in.

requirement: Run the project with no manual input; the system collects and analyzes automatically.
rationale: The user specified no manual input — all collection, analysis, and publishing must be automated.

requirement: Use a shared coordination board to manage tasks across parallel sessions and avoid conflicts.
rationale: Parallel sessions must coordinate via COORDINATION.md to avoid duplicate work and conflicts.
